newsitem.title: KENYA: Mobs kill six Kenya police at Mombasa.
newsitem.headline: Mobs kill six Kenya police at Mombasa.

text.p: Kenya police said on Thursday six officers and seven civilians were killed when mobs burned down a police station at the port city of Mombasa, stealing firearms and releasing prisoners.
Residents said the armed assailants attacked two police stations at Likoni on Wednesday night, blocking the ferry to Mombasa until dawn to prevent police sending reinforcements.

The motive for the stunning attack, close to Kenya's favourite tourist beaches on the Indian Ocean, was unclear. Some witnesses said they were local people taking reprisals against Likoni police for alleged brutality.
But it was too early to rule out a political motive.

Kenya's police commissioner, Duncan Wachira, was accompanied by top military and security officials when he flew to Mombasa from the capital Nairobi early on Thursday to head investigations, witnesses said.
A police statement in Mombasa said six officers and two of the arsonists were killed. It said several civilians were seriously injured and police firearms were stolen.
"A major security operation was immediately launched to net the culprits," the statement said.
The Kenya Broadcasting Corporation (KBC) said police had made at least 20 arrests.
Later Kenya's police spokesman, Peter Kimanthi, told reporters in Mombasa the death toll had risen to 13 but the number of dead police officers remained at six.
A Reuters correspondent in Mombasa who visited the morgue at Coast general hospital on Thursday counted the bodies of 10 victims of the violence. At least two were burned policemen.
There were no reports of casualties among thousands of foreign tourists in the Mombasa area.
But a group of German tourists, heading for a disco by bus, did a fast U-turn at Likoni on Wednesday when they nearly drove into a fusillade, witnesses said.

There was no immediate evidence of any political motive for the attacks. Pre-election tension is high in the East African country and two policemen died in political violence in and near the capital on August 8.

Foreign and Kenyan human rights groups have this year denounced the police as brutal and corrupt. Low pay is one of the reasons with junior officers saying they take home as little as 2,000 shillings ($28) a month for their dangerous work.

Wednesday night's attacks began at about 8.30 P.M. (1730 GMT) when the assailants raided the tourist police post at Likoni situated inside a cargo container. The post is at the landing point of the ferry from Mombasa Island, separated from Likoni by a narrow sea channel.
Witnesses said the mob then moved on to the Likoni police station about 300 metres (yards) from the ferry. They set the station on fire, released prisoners held there and stole weapons.
For several hours they prevented the ferry from Mombasa Island docking at Likoni, blocking police reinforcements.
The last time the area was hit by serious violence was in December 1992 when the local Digo people attacked settlers from other tribes in a row over a Likoni quarry.
Mombasa lies on the Indian Ocean and is about 500 km (310 miles) southeast of Nairobi.
